column1: # Held-out service-detect set for M1 (brief v4 section 4).
# Labels were assigned from the section 6 fee table in SKILL.md - i.e. from
# hospital policy - NOT by reading the token lists in scripts/qa_seeding.py.
# That ordering is the whole point of a held-out set: if the labels came from the
# regexes, the test would only prove the regexes match themselves.
# COLUMN free_allowed means "is a free-exam claim PERMITTED on this item", not
# "should the reply mention a free exam". Those differ: a kx question about
# recovery time permits a free-exam claim but does not call for one. Whether to
# mention it is editorial; whether it is allowed is the gate. The first version of
# this file conflated the two and produced 11 false misses.
# source column:
#   real      verbatim from a seeding_*.md output file in scratch/ (pre-fix corpus)
#   collision one of the 4 mandatory collision cases named in brief section 4 M1
#   written   written for this set to cover a bucket the local corpus does not reach
# NOTE ON COVERAGE: brief M1 asks for 20 real + 4 collision. Only 4 of the 217
# output files are on this machine, and they yield 14 fee-relevant real questions.
# The remaining 6 real slots are marked `written` rather than fabricated as real.
# When the full corpus is available, replace them with real questions and re-run.
# NOTE ON `none` vs `ambiguous`: P4 fires only when a condition token
# (cận|viễn|loạn|lão thị) is present with no intent. An item with no service token
# at all yields `none`. Both route to hotline, so the fee outcome is identical;
# they are kept distinct for diagnostics.
# NOTE ON PRE-OP vs POST-OP: "mổ cận xong cần kiêng cữ gì" and "mổ xong bao lâu
# đi làm lại" carry no post-op token - they read equally as someone pre-op asking
# what to expect. Labelled kx, not fu_dnd. Both tiers are free anyway, so the
# free-gate outcome does not depend on resolving the ambiguity.
